title: Sum of All Subset XOR Totals
description: The XOR total of a subset is defined as the bitwise XOR of all its elements, or `0` if the subset is empty. Given an array `nums` of non-negative integers, return the sum of the XOR totals for every one of the `2^n` subsets of `nums` (counting subsets with identical elements at different indices separately).
hints: Consider each bit position `b` independently: if no element has bit `b` set, it contributes `0`; if at least one element has bit `b` set, exactly half (`2^(n - 1)`) of all subsets have an odd number of 1s at bit `b`.
Therefore, the sum of all subset XOR totals equals `(nums[0] | nums[1] | ... | nums[n - 1]) << (n - 1)`.

examples.explanation: Subsets {}, {1}, {3}, {1, 3} have XOR totals 0, 1, 3, 2 whose sum is 6.
The bitwise OR of [5, 1, 6] is 7, and 7 * 2^(3 - 1) = 7 * 4 = 28.
The bitwise OR of [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] is 15, and 15 * 2^5 = 480.
